evaluations:
**Ouro UI** — Ouro UI is built explicitly around dual-audience interfaces: **Ouro HX** provides copy-in React 19 + Tailwind CSS v4 components on Base UI alongside `ouro-check` for automated browser/axe-core/layout audits, while **Ouro AX** provides `ax-command` (one declaration generating CLI parsing, `--json` output, actionable `Fix:` errors, and MCP tools), `ax-outcome`/`ax-wait`, and `ax-xray` conformance checking ([Ouro UI README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui), [Ouro AX docs](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax.md)). On native platforms, [Ouro UI for Apple](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple) shares core tokens and claims for SwiftUI (`OuroHX`), App Intents (`OuroAX` and `ouro-ax-xray`), jank detection (`OuroFeel`), and headless agent screen driving (`OuroReins`). Its main trade-offs are that web targets React 19 only, native support is currently Apple-only (`ouro-ui-apple` is pre-1.0 v0.3.x) with no Android/Jetpack Compose or React Native implementation, and the copy-in registry model requires manual diff/overwrite upgrades; adding Android Compose and React Native bindings would close the cross-platform gap.

**A2UI** — A2UI is a generative UI protocol and multi-language SDK stack (Core, Agent, and Renderer SDKs) that streams declarative JSON UI specs with strict catalog schemas and data bindings across Web (React, Lit, Angular), Flutter (`a2ui_flutter`), SwiftUI (`A2UISwiftUI`), and Jetpack Compose (`androidx.a2ui.compose` at v0.9.1) ([A2UI README](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui), [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)). It excels at cross-platform, security-first agent-to-user rendering, including MCP integration (`@a2ui/catalog-mcp`), but it is a protocol and renderer layer rather than a complete visual design system or an agent-side CLI/API/App Intents toolkit. Shipping a richer first-party design-token/component layer and bringing Jetpack Compose to parity with v1.0 would make it stronger as a standalone toolkit.

**json-render** — json-render lets you define a Zod-typed component and action catalog (`defineCatalog`), bind platform implementations (`defineRegistry`), and stream LLM-generated JSON specs (`SpecStream`) to React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, `@json-render/shadcn`, `@json-render/react-native`, terminal (`@json-render/ink`), chat cards, PDFs, email, and `@json-render/mcp` ([json-render README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). Its cross-platform reach is broad on the web and includes React Native, but it lacks native SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, and Flutter renderers, and it focuses on agent-generated UI rather than giving agents ergonomic CLI/API/App Intents surfaces. Adding first-party SwiftUI and Compose renderers plus agent-side tool conformance checks would address those gaps.

**CopilotKit** — CopilotKit is an agent-user interaction stack built on AG-UI, offering chat/copilot UIs, shared state (`useAgent`), human-in-the-loop workflows, frontend tools, WebMCP support, and three generative UI modes (AG-UI tool calls, A2UI 1.0, and MCP Apps) across React, Angular, Vue, React Native, and Slack/Teams Channels ([CopilotKit README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It is an orchestration and copilot UX layer rather than a foundational design system, and its native mobile story stops at React Native without SwiftUI, Compose, or Flutter SDKs. Pairing it with a full design system or adding native iOS/Android SDKs would resolve those limits.

**Vercel UI SDK** — Vercel UI SDK (`@ui-sdk/core`) models headless UI behaviors (focus, selection, popups, drag-and-drop) across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, with explicit coding-agent skills and runtime browser-agent control via `createAgent` (`snapshot()`/`act()`) and WebMCP ([Vercel UI SDK README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui), [UI SDK Docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)). However, it is currently in beta, web-only (no native mobile/desktop targets), and unstyled, so you must supply your own visual design system. Reaching GA, adding styled defaults, and targeting native platforms would address these gaps.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — Agent-native unifies app capabilities via `defineAction`, exposing the same Zod-validated function to React (`useActionQuery`) and to agents over tools, HTTP, MCP, A2A, and CLI, backed by shared database and application state ([Agent-native README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). While its shared-action architecture is well suited for human-and-agent workflows, it is an application framework rather than a visual design system and is web-focused (React hooks without official React Native or native mobile UI bindings). Adding native mobile UI bindings and a cohesive component token layer would address this.

**MCP Apps** — MCP Apps extends the Model Context Protocol so tools declare `ui://` HTML resources that render inline inside sandboxed iframes across compliant hosts like Claude, ChatGPT, and VS Code, with bidirectional tool/data messaging ([MCP Apps README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). It is a host-embedding protocol rather than a design system, and its iframe-based HTML model does not provide native SwiftUI, Compose, or React Native components. Combining it with a cross-platform design system or adding native host rendering primitives would be required for native apps.

**shadcn/ui** — shadcn/ui is an open-code React component distribution system and design system (Radix/Base UI + Tailwind CSS) with a flat-file registry, `llms.txt`, MCP server, and AI Elements patterns ([shadcn/ui README](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui), [shadcn/ui Docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs)). Its open-code model makes it easy for coding agents to read and author UI, but it is React web-only (no native iOS/Android/Flutter targets) and lacks runtime agent-interface primitives like CLI/MCP/App Intents parity. Extending its registry model to native platforms and runtime agent contracts would address those gaps.

**Tamagui** — Tamagui provides a universal styling system, optimizing compiler, and UI kit that shares code across React web and React Native, supplemented by `AGENTS.md`, `tamagui generate-prompt`, and GitMCP docs for coding agents ([Tamagui README](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). While strong for React/React Native UI sharing, its agent support is limited to coding-agent documentation rather than runtime interfaces that agents operate (no MCP, CLI, or generative UI protocol). Integrating a runtime agent-action or generative UI layer would close that gap.

**Flutter** — Flutter compiles Dart to native ARM machine code, WebAssembly/JS, and desktop from one codebase with hardware-accelerated rendering, and pairs with Google's GenUI SDK, Flutter AI Toolkit, and `a2ui_flutter` ([Flutter README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). Its trade-off for this goal is that Flutter Web renders to canvas/WASM rather than semantic DOM, complicating browser-agent inspection and WebMCP, and it lacks a built-in agent-surface conformance kit for CLI/MCP/system-intent parity. Exposing richer semantic/accessibility bridges on web and first-class agent action schemas would help.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — SwiftUI delivers declarative native UI across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS, and integrates with **App Intents** so Siri and Apple Intelligence can inspect entities and execute app actions ([SwiftUI Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). Its obvious constraint is platform lock-in to Apple ecosystems, with no web or Android story. Using it alongside a shared cross-platform token/protocol layer like Ouro UI or A2UI is needed for multi-platform reach.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — Material 3 in Jetpack Compose provides adaptive Android UI components, dynamic theming, and **AppFunctions** integration so on-device assistants like Gemini can discover and run app workflows ([Material 3 in Compose](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). Like SwiftUI, it is Android-centered (cross-platform web/iOS requires separate Compose Multiplatform tooling outside the core Android M3 docs). First-class web/iOS parity and unified MCP/CLI tooling would broaden its reach.

**Fluent UI** — Fluent UI offers mature, accessible React v9 (`@fluentui/react-components`) and Web Components in its main web repo, with separate platform libraries for React Native, Apple, Android, and WinUI ([Fluent UI README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). However, cross-platform code is split across separate repositories/APIs, and there is no built-in generative UI, MCP, or agent-interface layer. Unifying cross-platform bindings and adding agent-action primitives would address this.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Apps SDK UI is a curated React 18/19 + Tailwind 4 + Radix design system tailored for building ChatGPT Apps ([Apps SDK UI README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It is web-only (mobile ChatGPT renders responsive web widgets, with no React Native or native mobile SDK) and scoped specifically to ChatGPT app surfaces rather than general-purpose cross-platform or agent-operated CLI/API tooling. Generalizing beyond ChatGPT and adding native targets would be needed.

**AI Elements** — AI Elements provides shadcn/ui-based React components for AI chat, reasoning, and code blocks, but its standalone repo carries a deprecation notice for the end of November 2026 as patterns move into `shadcn/ui` ([AI Elements README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Beyond its deprecation, it is Next.js/React web-only and covers chat UI rather than native platforms or agent-usable interfaces. Adopting `shadcn/ui`'s built-in AI Elements avoids the deprecated package, though web-only limits remain.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Adobe's React Spectrum libraries pair WAI-ARIA-tested unstyled web hooks/components (React Aria) and Spectrum-styled web components with platform-agnostic state hooks (React Stately) ([React Spectrum README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). While React Stately can inform non-web state, React Aria and React Spectrum are web-only and offer no agent-facing runtime or generative UI layer. Adding native adapters and agent-action hooks would address this.

**Base UI** — Base UI delivers unstyled, accessible React web components with `llms.txt` and Markdown documentation for LLMs ([Base UI README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui), [Base UI Quick start](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start)). It is an unstyled web-only primitive layer—not a complete visual design system, native toolkit, or runtime agent interface—though it serves well as a foundation (as used by shadcn/ui and Ouro HX). Pairing it with styled tokens, native counterparts, and an agent layer is required.

**Radix UI** — Radix Primitives provides unstyled, accessible React web primitives for building design systems ([Radix Primitives README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It is web-only, unstyled, and includes no native mobile support or agent-facing capabilities. Like Base UI, it requires a styled token layer, native platform libraries, and separate agent tooling.

**MUI** — Material UI is a battle-tested React web implementation of Material Design with extensive enterprise components ([Material UI README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It is React web-only with no native mobile UI layer and no built-in agent-interface or generative UI primitives. Cross-platform and agent-facing capabilities would require separate toolkits.

**Chakra UI** — Chakra UI is an accessible React component system with an MCP server (`@chakra-ui/react-mcp`) aimed at helping coding agents use the library ([Chakra UI README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). It remains React web-only (no native iOS/Android/RN targets) and lacks runtime agent-operated interface primitives. Native targets and runtime agent contracts would address those gaps.
pullQuote: Ouro UI treats human screens and agent tools as one design system, pairing accessible web and SwiftUI components with automated conformance checks.
testimonial: I would choose Ouro UI because it is designed from the ground up for both audiences in the prompt: Ouro HX delivers accessible, responsive React and SwiftUI components for people, while Ouro AX gives agents `ax-command` (one definition for CLI, `--json`, and MCP tools) and `ax-xray` conformance checks so agent surfaces don't rot. On Apple platforms, `ouro-ui-apple` extends that same token and claim set into SwiftUI, App Intents verification (`ouro-ax-xray`), and `OuroReins` for headless agent screen driving. The honest trade-off compared to A2UI—which already ships official renderers for Flutter and Jetpack Compose alongside SwiftUI and web—is that Ouro UI's native support is currently Apple-only and pre-1.0, so Android would still require a separate layer today. Even so, having unified human and agent ergonomics with automated verification on both sides makes Ouro UI the strongest foundation.

actions.evaluations:
**Ouro UI** — Ouro UI is built explicitly around dual-audience interfaces: **Ouro HX** provides copy-in React 19 + Tailwind CSS v4 components on Base UI alongside `ouro-check` for automated browser/axe-core/layout audits, while **Ouro AX** provides `ax-command` (one declaration generating CLI parsing, `--json` output, actionable `Fix:` errors, and MCP tools), `ax-outcome`/`ax-wait`, and `ax-xray` conformance checking ([Ouro UI README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui), [Ouro AX docs](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax.md)). On native platforms, [Ouro UI for Apple](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple) shares core tokens and claims for SwiftUI (`OuroHX`), App Intents (`OuroAX` and `ouro-ax-xray`), jank detection (`OuroFeel`), and headless agent screen driving (`OuroReins`). Its main trade-offs are that web targets React 19 only, native support is currently Apple-only (`ouro-ui-apple` is pre-1.0 v0.3.x) with no Android/Jetpack Compose or React Native implementation, and the copy-in registry model requires manual diff/overwrite upgrades; adding Android Compose and React Native bindings would close the cross-platform gap.

**A2UI** — A2UI is a generative UI protocol and multi-language SDK stack (Core, Agent, and Renderer SDKs) that streams declarative JSON UI specs with strict catalog schemas and data bindings across Web (React, Lit, Angular), Flutter (`a2ui_flutter`), SwiftUI (`A2UISwiftUI`), and Jetpack Compose (`androidx.a2ui.compose` at v0.9.1) ([A2UI README](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui), [A2UI SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)). It excels at cross-platform, security-first agent-to-user rendering, including MCP integration (`@a2ui/catalog-mcp`), but it is a protocol and renderer layer rather than a complete visual design system or an agent-side CLI/API/App Intents toolkit. Shipping a richer first-party design-token/component layer and bringing Jetpack Compose to parity with v1.0 would make it stronger as a standalone toolkit.

**json-render** — json-render lets you define a Zod-typed component and action catalog (`defineCatalog`), bind platform implementations (`defineRegistry`), and stream LLM-generated JSON specs (`SpecStream`) to React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, `@json-render/shadcn`, `@json-render/react-native`, terminal (`@json-render/ink`), chat cards, PDFs, email, and `@json-render/mcp` ([json-render README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). Its cross-platform reach is broad on the web and includes React Native, but it lacks native SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, and Flutter renderers, and it focuses on agent-generated UI rather than giving agents ergonomic CLI/API/App Intents surfaces. Adding first-party SwiftUI and Compose renderers plus agent-side tool conformance checks would address those gaps.

**CopilotKit** — CopilotKit is an agent-user interaction stack built on AG-UI, offering chat/copilot UIs, shared state (`useAgent`), human-in-the-loop workflows, frontend tools, WebMCP support, and three generative UI modes (AG-UI tool calls, A2UI 1.0, and MCP Apps) across React, Angular, Vue, React Native, and Slack/Teams Channels ([CopilotKit README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It is an orchestration and copilot UX layer rather than a foundational design system, and its native mobile story stops at React Native without SwiftUI, Compose, or Flutter SDKs. Pairing it with a full design system or adding native iOS/Android SDKs would resolve those limits.

**Vercel UI SDK** — Vercel UI SDK (`@ui-sdk/core`) models headless UI behaviors (focus, selection, popups, drag-and-drop) across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, with explicit coding-agent skills and runtime browser-agent control via `createAgent` (`snapshot()`/`act()`) and WebMCP ([Vercel UI SDK README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui), [UI SDK Docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)). However, it is currently in beta, web-only (no native mobile/desktop targets), and unstyled, so you must supply your own visual design system. Reaching GA, adding styled defaults, and targeting native platforms would address these gaps.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — Agent-native unifies app capabilities via `defineAction`, exposing the same Zod-validated function to React (`useActionQuery`) and to agents over tools, HTTP, MCP, A2A, and CLI, backed by shared database and application state ([Agent-native README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). While its shared-action architecture is well suited for human-and-agent workflows, it is an application framework rather than a visual design system and is web-focused (React hooks without official React Native or native mobile UI bindings). Adding native mobile UI bindings and a cohesive component token layer would address this.

**MCP Apps** — MCP Apps extends the Model Context Protocol so tools declare `ui://` HTML resources that render inline inside sandboxed iframes across compliant hosts like Claude, ChatGPT, and VS Code, with bidirectional tool/data messaging ([MCP Apps README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). It is a host-embedding protocol rather than a design system, and its iframe-based HTML model does not provide native SwiftUI, Compose, or React Native components. Combining it with a cross-platform design system or adding native host rendering primitives would be required for native apps.

**shadcn/ui** — shadcn/ui is an open-code React component distribution system and design system (Radix/Base UI + Tailwind CSS) with a flat-file registry, `llms.txt`, MCP server, and AI Elements patterns ([shadcn/ui README](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui), [shadcn/ui Docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs)). Its open-code model makes it easy for coding agents to read and author UI, but it is React web-only (no native iOS/Android/Flutter targets) and lacks runtime agent-interface primitives like CLI/MCP/App Intents parity. Extending its registry model to native platforms and runtime agent contracts would address those gaps.

**Tamagui** — Tamagui provides a universal styling system, optimizing compiler, and UI kit that shares code across React web and React Native, supplemented by `AGENTS.md`, `tamagui generate-prompt`, and GitMCP docs for coding agents ([Tamagui README](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). While strong for React/React Native UI sharing, its agent support is limited to coding-agent documentation rather than runtime interfaces that agents operate (no MCP, CLI, or generative UI protocol). Integrating a runtime agent-action or generative UI layer would close that gap.

**Flutter** — Flutter compiles Dart to native ARM machine code, WebAssembly/JS, and desktop from one codebase with hardware-accelerated rendering, and pairs with Google's GenUI SDK, Flutter AI Toolkit, and `a2ui_flutter` ([Flutter README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). Its trade-off for this goal is that Flutter Web renders to canvas/WASM rather than semantic DOM, complicating browser-agent inspection and WebMCP, and it lacks a built-in agent-surface conformance kit for CLI/MCP/system-intent parity. Exposing richer semantic/accessibility bridges on web and first-class agent action schemas would help.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — SwiftUI delivers declarative native UI across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS, and integrates with **App Intents** so Siri and Apple Intelligence can inspect entities and execute app actions ([SwiftUI Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). Its obvious constraint is platform lock-in to Apple ecosystems, with no web or Android story. Using it alongside a shared cross-platform token/protocol layer like Ouro UI or A2UI is needed for multi-platform reach.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — Material 3 in Jetpack Compose provides adaptive Android UI components, dynamic theming, and **AppFunctions** integration so on-device assistants like Gemini can discover and run app workflows ([Material 3 in Compose](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). Like SwiftUI, it is Android-centered (cross-platform web/iOS requires separate Compose Multiplatform tooling outside the core Android M3 docs). First-class web/iOS parity and unified MCP/CLI tooling would broaden its reach.

**Fluent UI** — Fluent UI offers mature, accessible React v9 (`@fluentui/react-components`) and Web Components in its main web repo, with separate platform libraries for React Native, Apple, Android, and WinUI ([Fluent UI README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). However, cross-platform code is split across separate repositories/APIs, and there is no built-in generative UI, MCP, or agent-interface layer. Unifying cross-platform bindings and adding agent-action primitives would address this.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Apps SDK UI is a curated React 18/19 + Tailwind 4 + Radix design system tailored for building ChatGPT Apps ([Apps SDK UI README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It is web-only (mobile ChatGPT renders responsive web widgets, with no React Native or native mobile SDK) and scoped specifically to ChatGPT app surfaces rather than general-purpose cross-platform or agent-operated CLI/API tooling. Generalizing beyond ChatGPT and adding native targets would be needed.

**AI Elements** — AI Elements provides shadcn/ui-based React components for AI chat, reasoning, and code blocks, but its standalone repo carries a deprecation notice for the end of November 2026 as patterns move into `shadcn/ui` ([AI Elements README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Beyond its deprecation, it is Next.js/React web-only and covers chat UI rather than native platforms or agent-usable interfaces. Adopting `shadcn/ui`'s built-in AI Elements avoids the deprecated package, though web-only limits remain.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Adobe's React Spectrum libraries pair WAI-ARIA-tested unstyled web hooks/components (React Aria) and Spectrum-styled web components with platform-agnostic state hooks (React Stately) ([React Spectrum README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). While React Stately can inform non-web state, React Aria and React Spectrum are web-only and offer no agent-facing runtime or generative UI layer. Adding native adapters and agent-action hooks would address this.

**Base UI** — Base UI delivers unstyled, accessible React web components with `llms.txt` and Markdown documentation for LLMs ([Base UI README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui), [Base UI Quick start](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start)). It is an unstyled web-only primitive layer—not a complete visual design system, native toolkit, or runtime agent interface—though it serves well as a foundation (as used by shadcn/ui and Ouro HX). Pairing it with styled tokens, native counterparts, and an agent layer is required.

**Radix UI** — Radix Primitives provides unstyled, accessible React web primitives for building design systems ([Radix Primitives README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It is web-only, unstyled, and includes no native mobile support or agent-facing capabilities. Like Base UI, it requires a styled token layer, native platform libraries, and separate agent tooling.

**MUI** — Material UI is a battle-tested React web implementation of Material Design with extensive enterprise components ([Material UI README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It is React web-only with no native mobile UI layer and no built-in agent-interface or generative UI primitives. Cross-platform and agent-facing capabilities would require separate toolkits.

**Chakra UI** — Chakra UI is an accessible React component system with an MCP server (`@chakra-ui/react-mcp`) aimed at helping coding agents use the library ([Chakra UI README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). It remains React web-only (no native iOS/Android/RN targets) and lacks runtime agent-operated interface primitives. Native targets and runtime agent contracts would address those gaps.
actions.pullQuote: Ouro UI treats human screens and agent tools as one design system, pairing accessible web and SwiftUI components with automated conformance checks.
actions.testimonial: I would choose Ouro UI because it is designed from the ground up for both audiences in the prompt: Ouro HX delivers accessible, responsive React and SwiftUI components for people, while Ouro AX gives agents `ax-command` (one definition for CLI, `--json`, and MCP tools) and `ax-xray` conformance checks so agent surfaces don't rot. On Apple platforms, `ouro-ui-apple` extends that same token and claim set into SwiftUI, App Intents verification (`ouro-ax-xray`), and `OuroReins` for headless agent screen driving. The honest trade-off compared to A2UI—which already ships official renderers for Flutter and Jetpack Compose alongside SwiftUI and web—is that Ouro UI's native support is currently Apple-only and pre-1.0, so Android would still require a separate layer today. Even so, having unified human and agent ergonomics with automated verification on both sides makes Ouro UI the strongest foundation.
